question.leadin: Identify some people in the history of a certain empire that was neither holy nor Roman.
question.text: The "first German to be called emperor of Italy," this man solidified his power by defeating the Magyars at Lechfeld and the Obodrites at Recknitz and established the Holy Roman Empire.
question.clue: Much of his ruling strength came from his namesake system of installing his own bishops, and later in his rule, he deposed John XII in favor of Leo VIII for the papacy.

swap.text: Fredrick Barborossa occupied this position, which was elected to be the catholic ruler of the German principalities. Other holders of this position were Charles V and Otto the Great.
swap.clue: The Treaty of Pressburg invalidated this office after the battle of Austerlitz in 1806, and it was selected by seven electors after the 1356 Golden Bull.

question.leadin: One monarch with this name legendarily raised several children without human interaction in an attempt to find a universal natural language.
question.text: Give this regnal name of the victor of the Sixth Crusade. An earlier Holy Roman Emperor with this name was defeated at Legnano [le-NYA-no] by the Lombard League.
question.clue: Another ruler with this name promulgated the Constitutions of Melfi, a legal code for Sicily, and was known as "stupor mundi" or "wonder of the world".

swap.leadin: Name some leaders associated with the 3rd Crusade.
swap.text: This German Holy Roman Emperor attempted to lead an army of 150,000 into the Holy Land, however, he drowned when his horse slipped while crossing the Saleph River.
swap.clue: He attempted to suppress the revolt of the Lombard League twice; the second time, the head of the Guelphs, Henry the Lion, refused to assist him.

question.leadin: Answer the following about slave rebellions in the Western Hemisphere.
question.text: A slave rebellion named after this holiday on the island of Jamaica was led by preacher Samuel Sharpe and mobilized up to 60,000 slaves in 1831. Also known as the Baptist War, this holiday also names an Australian island south of the island of Java.
question.clue: British and German soldiers during World War I met in "no man's land" to celebrate this holiday.

swap.leadin: This man was killed after the Battle of Rain despite being tended by Gustavus Adolphus's personal physician.
swap.text: Name this commander, who was victorious at White Mountain, leading to the capture of Prague.
swap.answerHtml: Count of Tilly [or Johann Tserclaes, Graf von Tilly]
swap.clue: This man commanded the forces of the Holy Roman Empire during the battle. During the battle, cannons belonging to this man's forces were captured by the Swedes and started firing on his troops.

question.leadin: FTPE, name some rulers of the Holy Roman Empire.
question.text: The first Emperor of the Saxon dynasty, this man resurrected the Empire from the ashes of the Carolingians after his victory at Lechfeld over the Magyars.
question.answerHtml: Otto I the Great (need one or the other)
question.clue: After further rebellions by his son Ludolph and by Conrad the Red, this man terminated their powers at the Imperial Diet of Auerstadt.

swap.text: At Lutzen, Swedish forces defeated this capable Bohemian general. Emperor Ferdinand II had this man killed when he seemed likely to defect to the Protestant side.
swap.clue: This general who was killed by Walter Devereux after issuing the Second Pilsen Declaration in 1634. He lost the Battle of Lutzen.

question.text: The Guelphs grew out of the Lombard League, formed to resist this Holy Roman Emperor's influence in Italy. This emperor drowned in the Saleph River while leading the Third Crusade.
question.answerHtml: Frederick I [or Frederick Barbarossa; or Friedrich I; or Friedrich Barbarossa; prompt on Frederick; prompt on Freidrich]
question.clue: This man was forced to sign the Treaty of Venice following his defeat at the Battle of Legnano by the Lombard League.

swap.text: In 1469, Corvinus also was elected king of this kingdom in the modern Czech Republic. After a namesake war, Corvinus agreed to limit his rule of this kingdom to Moravia, Silesia, and Lusatia.
swap.clue: Holy Roman Emperor Matthias took control of this region after imprisoning his ailing brother, Rudolf II ("the-second").

question.text: Apart from Tilly, the main general of the imperial forces was this Czech nobleman, who was despised by both Protestants and Catholics, and who was eventually assassinated with the emperor's approval in 1634.
question.clue: This man's ardent opposition to the Edict of Restitution and his forced retreat at the Battle of Lutzen earned the ire of Ferdinand II, which culminated in the Holy Roman Emperor greenlighting his murder in 1634.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Lion of the north, Gustavus Adolphus.
swap.text: At Breitenfeld, Gustavus laid the smackdown on this Count who earlier fought for the Catholic League against Frederick the Winter King at White Mountain. He would be himself slain at the Battle of Rain.
swap.clue: This general on the Catholic side was this man presided over the alleged Sack of Magdeburg. He lost the Battle of Breitenfeld, and died after being wounded by a cannon ball at the Lech River.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the politics of the Holy Roman Empire.
question.text: A 1356 proclamation known by this name explicitly named the seven positions whose titles conferred elector status. A 1222 edict with this name ceded a number of rights to the Hungarian nobility.
question.answerHtml: Golden Bull [or Golden Bull of 1356; or Golden Bull of 1222; or chrysobull; prompt on “bull”]
question.clue: Emperor Frederic II was identified as the source of the 1218 one of Berne, considered a forgery, but definitely did issue one dealing with the holdings of Teutonic knights in Prussia named for the town of Rimini.

swap.leadin: Its chapel has a famous octagonal dome and its hot sulphur springs made it a popular nineteenth-century spa resort.
swap.text: Name this city that was the namesake of treaties ending the War of Devolution and the War of Austrian Succession. It was also the capital of the Carolingian empire of Charlemagne.
swap.clue: Ravenna's San Vitale was probably the model for this city's Palatine Chapel.

question.leadin: This group was defeated by the Utraquists at the Battle of Lipany.
question.text: Name this religious faction which demanded a return to Biblical authority and was named for the Bohemian city of their origin.
question.clue: This more radical Hussite faction that allowed married priests and abolished all but two sacraments. They opposed the Utraquists.

swap.text: This Duke of Saxony was father of Otto the Great. This man allegedly gained his epithet after he received word that he was crowned king while he was mending his bird nets.
swap.answerHtml: Henry the Fowler [Heinrich der Finkler; Heinrich der Vogler; prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: His wife accompanied him on his campaigns building monasteries, one of which was their burial site of Quedlinburg.

question.text: When the undefeated John Zizka was replaced by Procopius the Great as leader of the Taborite army, emperor Sigismund and the utraquists teamed up to smack him down in this 1434 battle also known as Cesky Brod.
question.clue: The Taborites were eventually defeated by an Utraquist coalition at this battle, after which they made peace with the Council of Basel via the Compact of Iglau.

swap.text: Much of the Hussites' military success under Zizka stemmed from his pioneering of this tactic, in which bow and pistol-armed soldiers would hide in the namesake vehicles, and then charge once enemy cavalry faltered.
swap.answerHtml: the Wagenburg [or wagon fort; accept the Tabor or Laager; do not accept the specifically Russian “gulai-gorod”; prompt on descriptions like “they tied wagons together"]

question.text: In 1633, Oxenstierna established this league which united the Swabian, Franconian, and Upper and Lower Rhenish Circles to provide support for a military under Swedish command. It met at the Council of Frankfurt, where Saxony and Brandenburg refused to join, and it dissolved soon after.
question.clue: Richelieu supported Axel Oxenstierna's efforts to create this league, an alliance between Sweden, France, and the German Protestant Princes. This league was crushed by the Catholics at the first Battle of Nordlingen.

swap.text: Frederick Barbarossa withdrew his support of Antipope Callixtus III after this 1176 battle, in which he was decisively defeated by Alberto da Guissano and the forces of the Lombard League.
swap.clue: The carroccio, an oxen-drawn war wagon topped with a sacred altar, was used at this 1176 battle, which prompted its loser to sign the Treaty of Venice.
